commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to f843f738 (#25196)

Updates torch-mlir from its October 29 upstream baseline to
[`llvm/torch-mlir@f843f738`](https://github.com/llvm/torch-mlir/commit/f843f7386b422477a1570307fa5e5c12527193e0),
using
[`iree-org/torch-mlir@68244564`](https://github.com/iree-org/torch-mlir/commit/68244564a58e6eb48f15460dff217c135da631f6)
(`sm-iree-integrates/torch-20261104`) adapted to IREE's current LLVM
revision.

On top of canonical torch-mlir, the integration branch carries only the
LLVM submodule bump, now pointing at IREE's current LLVM and StableHLO
pins. The previous pin carried no other adaptation patches, so none were
dropped.

The PT2E quantize/dequantize verifier from llvm/torch-mlir#4848 rejects
an out-of-range per-channel axis and a group size that does not divide
the last input dimension. `@out_of_range_axis` and
`@indivisible_group_size` in `quantization_to_linalg_ext.mlir` built
such IR and are removed.

ONNX op test expectations: no changes in the CPU or GPU configs.

Assisted by: Claude

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: setup_metadata

commit_message:
[Build][AMDGPU] Use bitcode from the official ROCM distribution (#25133)

With the sunset of the old artifacts from
`shark-infra/amdgpu-device-libs`, migrate to LLVM bitcode blobs from the
official distribution. The version shall be pinned in
`build_tools/third_party/amdgpu_device_libs/rocm_package.json`.

This increases the bitcode download to 146Mb (in comparison, the WASI
SDK weighs in at <120Mb). Considering we're only using less than 1Mb,
that's unfortunate, but at the moment it's the only way to use the
official maintained source.

Fixes #25131.

Assisted-by: Codex

---------

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
(cherry picked from commit a7168a786718455f177eb24d8c1a07ed56b9f414)

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to f843f738 (#25196)

Updates torch-mlir from its October 29 upstream baseline to
[`llvm/torch-mlir@f843f738`](https://github.com/llvm/torch-mlir/commit/f843f7386b422477a1570307fa5e5c12527193e0),
using
[`iree-org/torch-mlir@68244564`](https://github.com/iree-org/torch-mlir/commit/68244564a58e6eb48f15460dff217c135da631f6)
(`sm-iree-integrates/torch-20261104`) adapted to IREE's current LLVM
revision.

On top of canonical torch-mlir, the integration branch carries only the
LLVM submodule bump, now pointing at IREE's current LLVM and StableHLO
pins. The previous pin carried no other adaptation patches, so none were
dropped.

The PT2E quantize/dequantize verifier from llvm/torch-mlir#4848 rejects
an out-of-range per-channel axis and a group size that does not divide
the last input dimension. `@out_of_range_axis` and
`@indivisible_group_size` in `quantization_to_linalg_ext.mlir` built
such IR and are removed.

ONNX op test expectations: no changes in the CPU or GPU configs.

Assisted by: Claude

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: colab

commit_message:
[Build][AMDGPU] Use bitcode from the official ROCM distribution (#25133)

With the sunset of the old artifacts from
`shark-infra/amdgpu-device-libs`, migrate to LLVM bitcode blobs from the
official distribution. The version shall be pinned in
`build_tools/third_party/amdgpu_device_libs/rocm_package.json`.

This increases the bitcode download to 146Mb (in comparison, the WASI
SDK weighs in at <120Mb). Considering we're only using less than 1Mb,
that's unfortunate, but at the moment it's the only way to use the
official maintained source.

Fixes #25131.

Assisted-by: Codex

---------

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
(cherry picked from commit a7168a786718455f177eb24d8c1a07ed56b9f414)

commit_message:
[RVV] Enable SpaceMiT IME on K3 and require an exact VLEN for IME tiles

Detect the IME cores of SpacemiT K3 by running `riscv_hwprobe` over the
calling thread CPUs (probing all CPUs returns marchid -1 on SoCs with
mixed core types like K3), and recognise the X100 and A100 marchids.

One smt.vmadot computes a block whose size is fixed by VLEN, so each IME
tile is correct at one VLEN only. The zvl*b bits are minimums, so a
VLEN-1024 A100 core passed the zvl256b check and ran the 12x16x8 tile
with wrong results. The 12x16x8 and 24x32x16 checks now also require the
next zvl*b bit to be clear.

Tested on both SpaceMiT K3 (X100 and A100 cores) and K1 (X60).

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization (#24969)

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing layouts during global optimization makes that phase target
aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding tensor
graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their epilogues and
result unpacks.

Add `--iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling`. For a module with a
single target that supports host encoding materialization
(`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported`: llvm-cpu on x86_64 or AArch64
with the CPU encoding resolver and without inner-tiled layouts), and
with the default encoding strategy, the new pass:

1. normalizes contraction dimensions,
2. assigns and propagates encodings,
3. materializes them on the host,
4. records the target (#24968).

Other modules, and the padding encoding strategy, keep dispatch-time
data tiling. The route takes its operation families and encoding
strategy from the dispatch-creation data-tiling flags, passed down from
`Pipelines.cpp`, because unsupported modules fall back to that route.

**Behavior changes that are easy to miss.**
- The flag takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags,
so conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set.
- The target is recorded even when nothing was data-tiled, so
dispatch-time assignment stays off for that module.
- The early pipeline also runs `BubbleUpExpandShapes` and `SinkReshapes`
on eligible modules.
- For modules with the attribute, dispatch creation always enables
`fuse-mmt4d` and `fuse-data-tiled-convolution` (#24967), even if they
are set to false, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions.

**Relation to existing paths.** `--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` with
early materialization also materializes on the host, but it has no
contraction normalization or propagation, and its mmt4d ops are not
fused with their epilogues. Like that path, this one relies on
`MaterializeHostEncodingPass` and is restricted to single-target
modules. The layout decision is split between this pass,
`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported` and the dispatch-creation
passes that read the attribute, and it adds HAL and Codegen dependencies
to the global phases. TODOs (#25031) describe moving it into its own
component that decides per affinity.

**Performance** on an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32,
`--iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=host`, median of 10). HAL dispatches in
parentheses. x86_64 has not been measured.

| workload | dispatch-time data tiling | this PR |
`--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` |
|---|---|---|---|
| matmul 512x1024x1024 + bias + ReLU | 1.49 ms (4) | 1.50 ms (3) | 1.43
ms (4) |
| batch_matmul 16x256x512x256 + ReLU | 1.69 ms (3) | 1.68 ms (3) | 1.75
ms (4) |
| conv NHWC 1x58x58x64, 3x3x64x64 + ReLU | 10.5 ms (3) | 10.5 ms (3) |
5.68 ms (1)* |

On these workloads the new path is within noise of dispatch-time data
tiling, which already fuses epilogues inside encoded dispatches. *The
global-opt row does not data-tile the convolution, because
`--iree-dispatch-creation-experimental-set-data-tiling-ops` only affects
dispatch creation. On this machine the existing experimental convolution
data tiling is slower than direct convolution codegen, independent of
this PR.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization (#24969)

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing layouts during global optimization makes that phase target
aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding tensor
graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their epilogues and
result unpacks.

Add `--iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling`. For a module with a
single target that supports host encoding materialization
(`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported`: llvm-cpu on x86_64 or AArch64
with the CPU encoding resolver and without inner-tiled layouts), and
with the default encoding strategy, the new pass:

1. normalizes contraction dimensions,
2. assigns and propagates encodings,
3. materializes them on the host,
4. records the target (#24968).

Other modules, and the padding encoding strategy, keep dispatch-time
data tiling. The route takes its operation families and encoding
strategy from the dispatch-creation data-tiling flags, passed down from
`Pipelines.cpp`, because unsupported modules fall back to that route.

**Behavior changes that are easy to miss.**
- The flag takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags,
so conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set.
- The target is recorded even when nothing was data-tiled, so
dispatch-time assignment stays off for that module.
- The early pipeline also runs `BubbleUpExpandShapes` and `SinkReshapes`
on eligible modules.
- For modules with the attribute, dispatch creation always enables
`fuse-mmt4d` and `fuse-data-tiled-convolution` (#24967), even if they
are set to false, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions.

**Relation to existing paths.** `--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` with
early materialization also materializes on the host, but it has no
contraction normalization or propagation, and its mmt4d ops are not
fused with their epilogues. Like that path, this one relies on
`MaterializeHostEncodingPass` and is restricted to single-target
modules. The layout decision is split between this pass,
`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported` and the dispatch-creation
passes that read the attribute, and it adds HAL and Codegen dependencies
to the global phases. TODOs (#25031) describe moving it into its own
component that decides per affinity.

**Performance** on an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32,
`--iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=host`, median of 10). HAL dispatches in
parentheses. x86_64 has not been measured.

| workload | dispatch-time data tiling | this PR |
`--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` |
|---|---|---|---|
| matmul 512x1024x1024 + bias + ReLU | 1.49 ms (4) | 1.50 ms (3) | 1.43
ms (4) |
| batch_matmul 16x256x512x256 + ReLU | 1.69 ms (3) | 1.68 ms (3) | 1.75
ms (4) |
| conv NHWC 1x58x58x64, 3x3x64x64 + ReLU | 10.5 ms (3) | 10.5 ms (3) |
5.68 ms (1)* |

On these workloads the new path is within noise of dispatch-time data
tiling, which already fuses epilogues inside encoded dispatches. *The
global-opt row does not data-tile the convolution, because
`--iree-dispatch-creation-experimental-set-data-tiling-ops` only affects
dispatch creation. On this machine the existing experimental convolution
data tiling is slower than direct convolution codegen, independent of
this PR.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization (#24969)

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing layouts during global optimization makes that phase target
aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding tensor
graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their epilogues and
result unpacks.

Add `--iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling`. For a module with a
single target that supports host encoding materialization
(`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported`: llvm-cpu on x86_64 or AArch64
with the CPU encoding resolver and without inner-tiled layouts), and
with the default encoding strategy, the new pass:

1. normalizes contraction dimensions,
2. assigns and propagates encodings,
3. materializes them on the host,
4. records the target (#24968).

Other modules, and the padding encoding strategy, keep dispatch-time
data tiling. The route takes its operation families and encoding
strategy from the dispatch-creation data-tiling flags, passed down from
`Pipelines.cpp`, because unsupported modules fall back to that route.

**Behavior changes that are easy to miss.**
- The flag takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags,
so conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set.
- The target is recorded even when nothing was data-tiled, so
dispatch-time assignment stays off for that module.
- The early pipeline also runs `BubbleUpExpandShapes` and `SinkReshapes`
on eligible modules.
- For modules with the attribute, dispatch creation always enables
`fuse-mmt4d` and `fuse-data-tiled-convolution` (#24967), even if they
are set to false, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions.

**Relation to existing paths.** `--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` with
early materialization also materializes on the host, but it has no
contraction normalization or propagation, and its mmt4d ops are not
fused with their epilogues. Like that path, this one relies on
`MaterializeHostEncodingPass` and is restricted to single-target
modules. The layout decision is split between this pass,
`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported` and the dispatch-creation
passes that read the attribute, and it adds HAL and Codegen dependencies
to the global phases. TODOs (#25031) describe moving it into its own
component that decides per affinity.

**Performance** on an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32,
`--iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=host`, median of 10). HAL dispatches in
parentheses. x86_64 has not been measured.

| workload | dispatch-time data tiling | this PR |
`--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` |
|---|---|---|---|
| matmul 512x1024x1024 + bias + ReLU | 1.49 ms (4) | 1.50 ms (3) | 1.43
ms (4) |
| batch_matmul 16x256x512x256 + ReLU | 1.69 ms (3) | 1.68 ms (3) | 1.75
ms (4) |
| conv NHWC 1x58x58x64, 3x3x64x64 + ReLU | 10.5 ms (3) | 10.5 ms (3) |
5.68 ms (1)* |

On these workloads the new path is within noise of dispatch-time data
tiling, which already fuses epilogues inside encoded dispatches. *The
global-opt row does not data-tile the convolution, because
`--iree-dispatch-creation-experimental-set-data-tiling-ops` only affects
dispatch creation. On this machine the existing experimental convolution
data tiling is slower than direct convolution codegen, independent of
this PR.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[Python] Make the HAL bitmask enums IntEnums instead of IntFlags

#25163 made MemoryType, BufferCompatibility, BufferUsage and
MemoryAccess nanobind IntFlags. On Python 3.11.0 to 3.11.3,
`MemoryType.HOST_LOCAL | MemoryType.DEVICE_VISIBLE` then fails with
"ValueError: 86 is not a valid MemoryType". This breaks
DeviceArray.to_host() for buffers that cannot be mapped, and hal_test
and array_interop_test in the scheduled linux_arm64_clang job, which
uses Python 3.11.0.

To build the result of `|`, enum.Flag looks up each bit of its
single-bit mask as a member. Python 3.11.4 (gh-103365) moved that mask
from `_flag_mask_` to a new `_singles_mask_` and put the bits of all
members into `_flag_mask_`. nanobind, including the latest release
v3.1.0, fills `_flag_mask_` the 3.11.4 way on every Python version.
Older 3.11 releases then look up bits that only occur in multi-bit
members, such as 0x40 in HOST_LOCAL, and find no member.

Drop py::is_flag() from the four enums. As IntEnums they keep
`__index__`, which #25163 added, and `|` and `&` return plain ints, as
they did before #25163. The bindings take these values as ints, so
callers need no changes. The three enums that were IntFlags before
#25163 have no such multi-bit members and stay IntFlags.

The new test also checks that no flag enum has bits that only occur in
multi-bit members, so re-adding py::is_flag() to MemoryType fails on
every Python version, not only on 3.11.0 to 3.11.3.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

ranges don't overlap. We can use a temporary buffer for these aligned
copies and clean it up through the existing path.

commit_message:
[CI] Turn off ClangIR in the BYO LLVM build

llvm/llvm-project#221291 made ClangIR part of the default clang build,
and with it MLIR; the LLVM integrate in #25119 picked this up. Clang's
libraries then link MLIR libraries that none of the LLVM_DISTRIBUTIONS
in llvm_config.cmake export, so configuring LLVM fails with 62 errors
like:

  CMake Error: install(EXPORT "ClangDevelopmentTargets" ...) includes
  target "clangFrontendTool" which requires target "MLIRIR" that is not
  in any export set.

This has broken the scheduled linux_x64_clang_byollvm job since the
2026-10-26 run.

byo_llvm.sh builds MLIR in a separate step against the installed LLVM,
and IREE does not use ClangIR, so build clang without it, as before.
With this change, LLVM at the current pin configures without errors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

llvm/llvm-project#221291 made ClangIR part of the default clang build,
and with it MLIR; the LLVM integrate in #25119 picked this up. Clang's
libraries then link MLIR libraries that none of the LLVM_DISTRIBUTIONS
in llvm_config.cmake export, so configuring LLVM fails with 62 errors
like:

  CMake Error: install(EXPORT "ClangDevelopmentTargets" ...) includes
  target "clangFrontendTool" which requires target "MLIRIR" that is not
  in any export set.

This has broken the scheduled linux_x64_clang_byollvm job since the
2026-10-26 run.

byo_llvm.sh builds MLIR in a separate step against the installed LLVM,
and IREE does not use ClangIR, so build clang without it, as before.
With this change, LLVM at the current pin configures without errors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: pkgci_summary / summary

commit_message:
[CI] Skip tests that need non-X86 LLVM targets in the BYO LLVM build

ukernel_inlining.mlir, added in #24833, compiles for aarch64 and
riscv64, but byo_llvm.sh builds LLVM with only the X86 target. The test
has failed the scheduled linux_x64_clang_byollvm job since #24833
landed. Since 2026-10-26 that job fails earlier, while configuring LLVM.

Move the aarch64 and riscv64 RUN lines into their own tests, tag them
with the LLVM target they need, and exclude those tags in
build_and_test_byo_llvm.sh.

ukernel_inlining.mlir, added in #24833, compiles for aarch64 and
riscv64, but byo_llvm.sh builds LLVM with only the X86 target. The test
has failed the scheduled linux_x64_clang_byollvm job since #24833
landed. Since 2026-10-26 that job fails earlier, while configuring LLVM.

Move the aarch64 and riscv64 RUN lines into their own tests, tag them
with the LLVM target they need, and exclude those tags in
build_and_test_byo_llvm.sh.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: Test RISC-V 64 / riscv64-baremetal

commit_message:
[CI] Publish attestation bundles with release assets

OpenSSF Scorecard's Signed-Releases check only looks at the names of
release assets. It does not query GitHub's attestation API, so the build
provenance attestations of the release assets do not count, and IREE's
Signed-Releases score stays at 0. A release counts as signed once one
of its assets is a `.sigstore.json` file, so upload the Sigstore bundle
of each build job with the files it covers.

The bundles also let users and mirrors verify the assets offline,
without GitHub's attestation API:

  gh attestation verify <file> --bundle <bundle>.sigstore.json \
    --repo iree-org/iree \
    --signer-workflow iree-org/iree/.github/workflows/build_package.yml

Stable releases reuse the candidate's iree-dist tarballs, so the
candidate's bundles still verify them there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Keep math.roundeven native where LLVM lowers it to instructions

MathTransform has expanded `math.roundeven` into a software sequence on every
target except ROCm and WebGPU since 68439a0e on every llvm-cpu target.

Most CPU targets actually have an intruction: FRINTN on AArch64,
ROUNDPS/ROUNDPD on x86 with SSE4.1, FCVT on riscv64 with D extension.

Since `math.roundeven` affects a lot of float-to-int quantization cases,
so it makes sense to use instructions and not software sequences wherever
possible.

Tests:
- New lit cases cover each target used in the check
- Numerical results are identical to before the change for f32 and f64,
  checked on x86, AArch64 (QEMU) and riscv64 hardware (SpacemiT K3).

Assisted-By: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Keep math.roundeven native where LLVM lowers it to instructions

MathTransform has expanded `math.roundeven` into a software sequence on every
target except ROCm and WebGPU since 68439a0e on every llvm-cpu target.

Most CPU targets actually have an intruction: FRINTN on AArch64,
ROUNDPS/ROUNDPD on x86 with SSE4.1, FCVT on riscv64 with D extension.

Since `math.roundeven` affects a lot of float-to-int quantization cases,
so it makes sense to use instructions and not software sequences wherever
possible.

Tests:
- New lit cases cover each target used in the check
- Numerical results are identical to before the change for f32 and f64,
  checked on x86, AArch64 (QEMU) and riscv64 hardware (SpacemiT K3).

target except ROCm and WebGPU since 68439a0e on every llvm-cpu target.

Most CPU targets actually have an intruction: FRINTN on AArch64,
ROUNDPS/ROUNDPD on x86 with SSE4.1, FCVT on riscv64 with D extension.

Since `math.roundeven` affects a lot of float-to-int quantization cases,
so it makes sense to use instructions and not software sequences wherever
possible.

Tests:
- New lit cases cover each target used in the check
- Numerical results are identical to before the change for f32 and f64,
  checked on x86, AArch64 (QEMU) and riscv64 hardware (SpacemiT K3).

copies and clean it up through the existing path.

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to f843f738 (#25196)

Updates torch-mlir from its October 29 upstream baseline to
[`llvm/torch-mlir@f843f738`](https://github.com/llvm/torch-mlir/commit/f843f7386b422477a1570307fa5e5c12527193e0),
using
[`iree-org/torch-mlir@68244564`](https://github.com/iree-org/torch-mlir/commit/68244564a58e6eb48f15460dff217c135da631f6)
(`sm-iree-integrates/torch-20261104`) adapted to IREE's current LLVM
revision.

On top of canonical torch-mlir, the integration branch carries only the
LLVM submodule bump, now pointing at IREE's current LLVM and StableHLO
pins. The previous pin carried no other adaptation patches, so none were
dropped.

The PT2E quantize/dequantize verifier from llvm/torch-mlir#4848 rejects
an out-of-range per-channel axis and a group size that does not divide
the last input dimension. `@out_of_range_axis` and
`@indivisible_group_size` in `quantization_to_linalg_ext.mlir` built
such IR and are removed.

ONNX op test expectations: no changes in the CPU or GPU configs.

Assisted by: Claude

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
